profile.about_headline: Curious About the Why Behind the Data
profile.about_text:
I’ve always been more interested in “why?” than simply knowing “what?”. With a background in Computer Science and AI & ML, I found my interest growing toward data analytics—turning raw information into clear insights and meaningful decisions.

I work with SQL, Python, Power BI, Tableau, and Excel to explore data, find patterns, build dashboards, and solve practical problems. I’m still early in my career, but I’m curious, hands-on, and constantly learning.

For me, analytics is not just about using tools. It’s about asking the right questions, validating the data, finding the story, and making the insight useful.

projects.title: Insight360 — Enterprise Analytics for Customer Retention, Service Excellence & Workforce Inclusion
projects.short_description: A 3-dashboard Power BI project analyzing 12,543 records across customer service, customer churn, and workforce diversity to turn operational data into practical business insights.
projects.full_description:
Insight360 brings together three different business perspectives in one analytics project: customer service performance, customer retention and churn, and workforce diversity & inclusion. I worked with 12,543 records across the three datasets, cleaned and transformed the data, created KPIs and interactive Power BI dashboards, and used the results to explore patterns that could support better business decisions.

The project was built as part of the PwC Switzerland Power BI Virtual Experience Program and focuses on going beyond simply presenting charts—using data to understand what is happening and where there may be opportunities for improvement
projects.category: Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, Power BI
projects.problem_statement: Customer operations, retention, and workforce data can contain thousands of individual records, making it difficult to quickly identify the patterns that matter. The challenge was to turn these separate datasets into clear dashboards that make performance, risk areas, and workforce trends easier to understand.
projects.objective:
Analyze customer service performance
Understand customer churn and retention
Identify patterns associated with customer loss
Explore workforce composition and diversity
Analyze hiring and promotion patterns
Build interactive KPI dashboards for decision-making
projects.dataset:
5,000 call-centre records
7,043 customer records
500 workforce records
12,543 total records
projects.methodology:
Data inspection → Data cleaning → Power Query transformation → Data modeling → DAX calculations → KPI development → Dashboard creation → Trend analysis → Business interpretation 
I focused on three analytical questions:

1. Customer Service:
How efficiently are calls being answered and resolved, and what does customer satisfaction look like?

2. Customer Retention:
How many customers are leaving, what contract patterns exist, and which customer behaviors deserve closer attention?

3. Workforce Inclusion:
How is the workforce distributed, and what do hiring, promotion, and representation patterns look like?
projects.key_findings:
Customer Service

Out of 5,000 calls, 4,054 were answered.
3,646 calls were marked as resolved.
Average customer satisfaction was 3.40/5.
Average answer speed was approximately 67.5 seconds.

Customer Retention

1,869 of 7,043 customers were classified as churned.
The overall churn rate was 26.54%.
Month-to-month contracts represented 3,875 customers, making this the largest contract group.
Average customer tenure was approximately 32.4 months.

Diversity & Inclusion

The dataset contains 500 employees.
205 employees were female and 295 were male.
51 employees received a promotion in FY21.
66 employees were recorded as new hires in FY20.
47 employees were recorded as FY20 leavers.
projects.business_impact:
The project does not claim a financial ROI because no real monetary return was generated or measured.

Instead, the measurable value of the project is demonstrated through the analysis itself:

12,543 total records analyzed
3 business areas
3 datasets
3 Power BI dashboards
5,000 customer-service records
7,043 customer records
500 workforce records
1,869 churned customers identified
4,054 answered calls analyzed
3,646 resolved calls analyzed
51 FY21 promotions analyzed

The dashboards turn these datasets into a more accessible view of service performance, customer retention, and workforce trends, helping demonstrate how Power BI can translate raw business data into decision-support information.

projects.title: T20 Cricket Batsmen Performance Analysis
projects.short_description: A Power BI dashboard that turns T20 batting data into a simple view of runs, strike rate, boundaries, and overall player performance.
projects.full_description: I built this project to explore what makes a T20 batsman stand out. Instead of looking at runs alone, I combined multiple batting metrics to compare players, spot consistent performers, and understand how scoring style changes across players.
projects.category: Data Analytics • Power BI • Sports Analytics
projects.problem_statement: T20 cricket moves quickly, and a player's total runs don't always tell the full story. A batsman scoring 40 runs at a high strike rate can have a very different impact from someone scoring the same runs more slowly.
projects.objective:
Compare batsmen across key performance metrics
Identify high-scoring and efficient players
Analyze boundary-hitting patterns
Understand consistency and scoring contribution
Present the analysis through an interactive dashboard
projects.dataset:
Player-level T20 batting statistics covering multiple performance indicators, including:

Runs
Matches
Innings
Balls Faced
Batting Average
Strike Rate
Fours
Sixes
Dismissals
projects.methodology: Data Cleaning → Power Query → DAX Measures → KPI Creation → Player Comparison → Performance Analysis → Interactive Power BI Dashboard
projects.key_findings:
The dashboard focuses on 8+ core batting metrics, including:

Total Runs — overall scoring contribution
Strike Rate — scoring speed
Batting Average — consistency
Runs per Innings — typical scoring contribution
4s & 6s — boundary-hitting ability
Boundary Runs — contribution from boundaries
Balls Faced — batting workload
Dismissals—performance context
projects.business_impact: The project turns detailed player statistics into an easy-to-read performance view. Instead of manually comparing several numbers for every player, users can quickly explore the metrics that matter and identify different types of performers.

snapshot.title: SQL Business Insights & SaaS Churn Diagnostics
snapshot.short_description: Diagnostic SQL engine analyzing 450K+ subscription records to detect early churn warning signals and protect annual recurring revenue.
snapshot.full_description: A comprehensive end-to-end SQL diagnostic model built for subscription SaaS metrics. The system tracks Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) expansion, contraction, and cohort retention decay curves, alerting account managers 60 days before contract renewal.
snapshot.problem_statement: A subscription SaaS company experienced an undetected 18% quarterly revenue contraction due to silent churn in mid-tier enterprise accounts without proactive visibility.
snapshot.objective: Design an automated SQL diagnostic model to track monthly recurring revenue (MRR) cohorts and identify leading indicators of customer churn 60 days prior to contract renewal.
snapshot.dataset: 450,000+ subscription transaction records, user event logs, and billing logs spanning 24 months across 1,200 enterprise and mid-market accounts.
snapshot.methodology: Engineered recursive SQL CTEs and rolling window functions to partition user engagement by weekly active utilization. Constructed cohort retention heatmaps and calculated feature-level drop-off rates.
snapshot.key_findings: Accounts with <3 weekly active users in their first 30 days had a 72% likelihood of churn by month 6. Feature unbundling in Q2 caused a 24% drop in core analytics usage among non-technical admins.
snapshot.business_impact: Enabled the customer success team to proactively intervene on at-risk accounts, reducing voluntary churn by 14.5% and preserving $185,000 in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR).
